question.text: An investor currently earns Rs. 1,20,000 per month. His income is expected to grow at 8% per annum. He plans to retire in 15 years. Using the replacement ratio method with a 75% replacement ratio, what will be his required annual income in the first year of retirement?

explanation.text: The Logic: Current annual income = Rs. 1,20,000 x 12 = Rs. 14,40,000. Projected annual income at retirement = Rs. 14,40,000 x (1.08)^15 = Rs. 14,40,000 x 3.172169 ≈ Rs. 45,67,924. Applying the 75% replacement ratio: 0.75 x 45,67,924 ≈ Rs. 34,25,942. The Trap: Rs. 10,80,000 and Rs. 14,40,000 trap candidates who apply the replacement ratio to current income without projecting growth over 15 years; Rs. 38,05,265 results from using 100% replacement instead of 75%. Note: The replacement ratio is applied to the income projected to the retirement date, not to today's income.
